title: Comparing more precisely
goal: Weigh two options in detail: *lika … som* and *inte lika … som*, *mer* and *mest* with long adjectives, comparing *how* you do things (*fortare, oftare*) and saying something keeps improving (*allt bättre*).
bekal: you can say "as … as", "not quite as … as" and "twice as … as"
you can compare long adjectives with *mer / mest*: *mer intressant*, *mer flexibelt*
you can compare adverbs (*fortare, oftare, långsammare*) and say *allt bättre*, *mer och mer*
wave: Go back to Unit 8: make five sentences that give a reason with *eftersom*, then turn each one round into a result with *därför* + inverted verb (*Eftersom jag var trött…* → *Därför gick jag hem*).

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Kaféet eller bokhandeln?
dialogs.intro: Dian has been offered two part-time jobs: one at a small café on Södermalm, run by a woman called Maja, and one at a big bookshop in the city center. Over coffee at the kitchen table, Elin helps her decide.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Nå? Har du bestämt dig? Kaféet eller bokhandeln?
lines.id: Well? Have you made up your mind? The café or the bookshop?
lines.literal: well? have you decided yourself? café-the or bookshop-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Inte än. Bokhandeln betalar lite bättre, men kaféet ligger mycket närmare.
lines.id: Not yet. The bookshop pays a bit better, but the café is much closer.
lines.literal: not yet. bookshop-the pays a-little better, but café-the lies much nearer.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Kaféet är fem minuter bort. Till bokhandeln tar det dubbelt så lång tid.
lines.id: The café is five minutes away. To the bookshop it takes twice as long.
lines.literal: café-the is five minutes away. to bookshop-the takes it double so long time.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och lönen? Är den lika bra på kaféet som i bokhandeln?
lines.id: And the pay? Is it as good at the café as at the bookshop?
lines.literal: and wage-the? is it equally good at café-the as in bookshop-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Nej, inte riktigt lika bra. Men på kaféet får jag dricks.
lines.id: No, not quite as good. But at the café I get tips.
lines.literal: no, not really equally good. but at café-the get I tips.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Vilket jobb är mer intressant, då?
lines.id: Which job is more interesting, then?
lines.literal: which job is more interesting, then?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bokhandeln, förstås. Men kaféet är mer flexibelt. Där kan jag jobba när jag inte har lektioner.
lines.id: The bookshop, of course. But the café is more flexible. There I can work when I don't have classes.
lines.literal: bookshop-the, of-course. but café-the is more flexible. there can I work when I not have lessons.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Och Maja, chefen? Hon verkade jättetrevlig.
lines.id: And Maja, the boss? She seemed really nice.
lines.literal: and Maja, boss-the? she seemed giant-nice.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det är hon. Och hon pratar långsammare än alla andra i Stockholm!
lines.id: She is. And she speaks more slowly than everyone else in Stockholm!
lines.literal: that is she. and she talks slower than all others in Stockholm!

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Din svenska blir allt bättre. Snart pratar du lika fort som hon.
lines.id: Your Swedish keeps getting better. Soon you'll be talking as fast as she does.
lines.literal: your Swedish becomes ever better. soon talk you equally fast as she.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Knappast! Men jag förstår mer och mer, och jag pratar svenska oftare nu än i höstas.
lines.id: Hardly! But I understand more and more, and I speak Swedish more often now than last fall.
lines.literal: hardly! but I understand more and more, and I talk Swedish more-often now than in autumn-last.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Då tycker jag att du ska ta kaféet. Där pratar du med folk hela dagen.
lines.id: Then I think you should take the café. There you'll be talking to people all day.
lines.literal: then think I that you shall take café-the. there talk you with people whole day-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Du har rätt. Ju mer jag pratar, desto bättre blir jag.
lines.id: You're right. The more I talk, the better I get.
lines.literal: you have right. the more I talk, the better become I.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Exakt. Ring Maja nu, innan du ändrar dig!
lines.id: Exactly. Call Maja now, before you change your mind!
lines.literal: exactly. ring Maja now, before you change yourself!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Okej, jag ringer. Hjälp, jag är nervösare än före en tenta!
lines.id: Okay, I'll call. Help, I'm more nervous than before an exam!
lines.literal: okay, I ring. help, I am more-nervous than before an exam!

notes: **Är den lika bra … som …?** — *lika* + adjective + *som* is "as … as": *lika bra som*, *lika fort som*. To deny it, put *inte* in front: *inte lika bra* (not as good); *inte riktigt lika bra* softens it to "not quite as good" — the polite Swedish way to say something is worse. **Dubbelt så lång tid** is "twice as long": here Swedish uses *så*, just as English does.

**Mer intressant, mer flexibelt** — long adjectives, and above all loanwords and adjectives ending in *-isk*, are compared with *mer* and *mest* instead of *-are* and *-ast*, exactly like English "more interesting". The adjective still agrees with its noun: *kaféet* is an *ett*-word, so *mer flexib**elt***.

**Lite bättre, mycket närmare** — to say "a bit better" or "much closer", put *lite* or *mycket* before the comparative. Never *mer* — *mer bättre* is as wrong in Swedish as "more better" is in English. For "even better", use *ännu*: *ännu bättre*.

**Långsammare, fortare, oftare** — adverbs compare just like adjectives: *fort – fortare – fortast*, *ofta – oftare – oftast*, *långsamt – långsammare – långsammast*. Watch the double *m*: *långsam* + *-are* = *långsa**mm**are*, the same doubling you saw in *gammal* → *gamla* in reverse.

**Allt bättre, mer och mer** — two ways to say something keeps growing: *allt* + comparative (*allt bättre*, *allt oftare*) or the comparative twice with *och* (*bättre och bättre*, *mer och mer*). And a preview: **Ju mer jag pratar, desto bättre blir jag** is "the more…, the better…". After *desto* + comparative, the verb comes next: *desto bättre **blir jag***.

**Dricks** ("tips") is never required in Sweden, since service is included in the price, but in cafés there is often a jar by the till and customers round up when paying by card. **Nervösare** or **mer nervös**? Both are correct — a handful of adjectives allow both. And **ändra sig** (change your mind) is another reflexive verb for your Unit 7 collection.

grammars.title: As … as, not as … as, twice as …
body: Swedish compares equal things with *lika … som*. Every pattern below keeps the adjective in its basic form and joins the second part with *som*.
after: In careful Swedish, a pronoun after *som* or *än* stays in the subject form: *lika fort som **hon***, *äldre än **jag***. In everyday speech you will hear *än mig* and *som henne* all the time; both pass, but write *jag* and *hon*.
Unequal comparisons use *än* (than), as you learned in Svenska 101: *Kaféet ligger närmare **än** bokhandeln.*

grammars.title: -are or mer?
body: Most short, common adjectives take *-are / -ast*. Long adjectives, loanwords and a few special endings take *mer / mest*. If you're unsure, *mer / mest* is never a disaster, but *-are* on a long word often sounds odd.
after: Never combine the two: *mer billigare* is wrong, just like "more cheaper".
In the definite form (Unit 9), the superlative takes *-e* after *-ast*, and *mest* is followed by the *-a* form: *den billig**aste** lampan*, *det **mest** intressant**a** jobbet*.

blocks.text: Adverbs tell you *how*, *how often* or *how much*, and they compare just as adjectives do. Several of the most common ones are irregular — you already know some of them from *bra – bättre – bäst*.

blocks.title: Gärna, hellre, helst — saying what you prefer
items: *Jag dricker **gärna** te.* — I like drinking tea.
*Jag dricker **hellre** te än kaffe.* — I'd rather drink tea than coffee.
*Jag dricker **helst** grönt te.* — I prefer green tea most of all.
This is the most natural way to talk about preferences in Swedish — much more common than *föredra*.

blocks.text: Many students in Sweden have a *deltidsjobb* or an *extrajobb* in a café, shop or warehouse. Pay is usually set by a collective agreement, *kollektivavtal*, between unions and employers — Sweden has no legal minimum wage, but the agreements play that role. The question Swedes ask first about a job is often not the pay but *Hur är schemat?* — what the schedule looks like.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 9
items: Compare things you own with *den här* / *den där*: *Den här lilla lampan är billigare än den där gamla.* *Min nya cykel är snabbare än min gamla.*
Then use *hela* and *halva*: *Det nya jobbet tar halva tiden.* *Jag pratar svenska hela dagen nu.*

exercises.prompt: Write the comparative of the word in brackets, with *-are* or with *mer*. Make it agree where needed.
items: Bokhandeln betalar ____ än kaféet. (bra)
Kaféet ligger ____ än bokhandeln. (nära)
Den här boken är ____ än den där. (intressant)
Maja pratar ____ än Elin. (långsamt)
Jag pratar svenska ____ nu än förra året. (ofta)
Ett jobb på kafé är ____ än ett jobb i en bokhandel. (flexibel)
Att cykla är ____ än att ta bussen. (praktisk)
Lönen är inte ____ bra som i bokhandeln.
Jonas är lika lång ____ Lars.
Elin är två år äldre ____ Jonas.
Det tar dubbelt ____ lång tid med buss.
Din svenska blir ____ bättre.
